title: BindableEvent
summary: Same-side messaging between scripts: Fire() and .Event let Scripts talk to Scripts (or LocalScripts to LocalScripts). It does NOT cross the client/server boundary — use RemoteEvent for that.

methods.name: Fire
methods.description: Fires the event to all connections on THIS side (no network involved).

events.name: Event
events.description: Receives whatever Fire sent. Note: the event member is literally named Event.

details.heading: Tables are deep-copied
details.body: Arguments pass through serialization even on the same machine: tables arrive as deep copies with metatables stripped. Mutations on the receiver never affect the sender's table.

explanation.whatItIs: A private intercom for scripts that run in the same world — no network, no player parameter. 'Hey other server script, the round just ended.'
explanation.whyItExists: Decoupling: systems can broadcast facts ('GamePhaseChanged') without knowing who's listening.
whenToUse: Broadcasting game-phase changes between server modules/scripts
Loose coupling between independent systems on the same side
When a ModuleScript-based Signal implementation isn't available in your project
whenNotToUse: Client ↔ server — BindableEvent never crosses that line; use RemoteEvent
Simple function calls between your own modules — just call the function; bindables add indirection
Performance-sensitive per-frame signals (table copying costs; prefer direct calls or a custom Signal)
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
Script A:  bindable:Fire("RoundEnd", scores)
                              │ (same machine, same runtime)
Script B:  bindable.Event:Connect(function(msg, scores) ... end)
```
Like RemoteEvent, minus the network, minus the player parameter.
tips: In modern codebases many teams use a custom Signal module or a simple callbacks table instead — fewer surprises with table copying
Keep BindableEvents where both scripts can reach them (ServerScriptService for server-side ones)
commonMistakes: Trying to use BindableEvent for client/server messaging — it silently stays on one side
Expecting the receiver to see the SAME table you fired — it's a copy, metatables gone

examples.title: Round system broadcasting phases
examples.code:
-- == ServerScriptService/Signals/RoundEvents (BindableEvent) ==

-- RoundManager Script:
local roundEvents = script.Parent.Parent.Signals.RoundEvents
roundEvents:Fire("PhaseChanged", "Intermission", 15)

-- Some other Script that cares:
local roundEvents = game:GetService("ServerScriptService").Signals.RoundEvents
roundEvents.Event:Connect(function(message, phase, duration)
    if message == "PhaseChanged" then
        print("New phase:", phase, "for", duration, "seconds")
    end
end)
